Subject: High 429 spike and timeouts during nightly billing run

Laura —

Heads up: during our scheduled nightly billing pipeline (00:00–02:00 ET) we saw a sustained spike of 429s and client-side timeouts that caused the downstream aggregator to drop ~18% of invoices. The problem started at approximately 00:07 ET and persisted for ~45 minutes with several retry storms from our end. We attached a subset of request traces and the billing manifest for the affected run.

Symptoms: 1) token-level 429s (quota exceeded) coming back from the Redwood API; 2) elevated p95 latency on the first token for requests that did not 429; 3) our retry backoff didn't fully dampen due to misclassification of the error as transient in our client.

Can you confirm whether there was any code/config change or cutover on your side around 00:00 ET? We're on a tight go-live schedule and this blocked reconciliation jobs for a major customer segment.

(attachment: nightly_run_20261118_request_trace.log)

—Dana

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:32:41 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: High 429 spike — initial triage notes

Folks — quick triage notes from Evelyn and infra:

Evelyn’s findings (summarized):
- At 00:06:45 ET a quota policy push executed for org "brighthealth-prod" as part of an automated tiering cutover (intent: roll customers onto new per-project caps). The push incorrectly mapped a subset of projects to the "standard-lite" bucket (per-project cap = 1/10th of expected).
- The misapplied mapping tracked back to a stale join key in the migration mapping table (quota_mapping_snapshot_20261118.json attached).
- Requests from bh-billing-prod-01 immediately hit per-project limits and returned 429s. BrightHealth’s client retried aggressively with short backoff which amplified the spike.

Proposed immediate mitigations (we executed #1 already):
1) Roll back the recent mapping push for brighthealth-prod (COMPLETED @ 00:28 ET).
2) Create a temporary override for org brighthealth-prod to raise per-project cap to pre-cutover levels for the next 24 hours (IN PROGRESS).
3) Add on-the-fly token-level throttling (soft limit) to protect control-plane from retry storms.
4) Postmortem: migration script needs additional safety checks — stop-on-mismatch and a dry-run verification.

Attachments: quota_mapping_snapshot_20261118.json, billing_run_manifest.csv

Rishi
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Subject: Urgent: Exec brief — BrightHealth major 429 incident impacting billing (need decision on credits & SLA)

Jonas —

Summary (TL;DR):
- Incident: brighthealth-prod experienced sustained 429s during nightly billing (00:07–00:52 ET). Root cause: automated quota tiering cutover incorrectly mapped some projects to the "standard-lite" bucket (lower per-project caps).
- Impact: BrightHealth reported ~18% of invoices dropped/rescheduled, finance reconciliation delayed, and an on-call pager storm for their ops team. They are escalated to execs and asking for remediation + credit.
- What we did: rolled back mapping at 00:28 ET, applied a 24h override on per-project caps, and applied temporary soft-throttles to reduce retry amplification. Incident is contained; error rate returned to baseline by 00:52 ET.

Decisions needed from leadership:
1) Commercial remediation: recommend a goodwill credit (proposed: one month of usage credit for affected environments OR a $40k one-time credit). We should be prepared to negotiate.
2) SLA exception: offer elevated support for 90 days (dedicated customer success touchpoints + extended retention for their logs).
3) Operational change: approve expedited postmortem and a hold on further quota cutovers until migration script remediation is complete.

I recommend approval for the proposed credit + immediate communication to the customer summarizing root cause and timeline for fixes.

—Laura
